Did you Know?
Pakistan is home to versatile and potent wildlife,
which sadly, is running low in numbers. Endangered
species all over the world get special attention and
security - whilst the Pakistani animals strive to
survive in these challenging conditions.
Let's take a look at some of these amazing animals
that are in the danger of extinction.
Indus River Dolphin
Indus river dolphins are believed to have originated in the
ancient Tethys Sea. When the sea dried up approximately
50 million years ago, the dolphins were forced to adapt to
its only remaining habitat--rivers.
The Indus River Dolphin is found in the Lower Indus Basin.
These friendly creatures are often seen jumping around
boats and putting on performances for anyone that wants
to watch.
Woolly Flying Squirrel
The Gilgit region is home to the nocturnal rodent, Woolly
Flying Squirrel. This unique creature looks like a bat but is
actually a squirrel. The flying squirrel is one of the largest
squirrels in the world with 1.5 to 2 feet in height. Due to
loss of natural habitat they are now labeled as critically
endangeredspecies.
